sentences.english: The bird searches for water.
The bird makes for the river.
Near the river, the bird sees a girl.
The girl has water.
The girl gives the bird the water.
The bird takes the water.
The bird carries the water to the forest.
And so the bird loves the girl.
The girl guards the bird.
The bird loves the faithful girl.
The small yet strong husband has a wife.
sentences.latin: Marītus parvus sed fortis uxōrem habet.

sentences.english: The wife carries many books to the table.
sentences.latin: Uxor multōs librōs ad mēnsam portat.

sentences.english: The husband lifts the many books.
And so the wife gives the husband a new book.
sentences.latin: Itaque uxor marītō librum novum dat.

sentences.english: The husband has the new book.
In the field, the wife sees a heavy table.
sentences.latin: In agrō uxor mēnsam gravem videt.

sentences.english: The husband lifts the heavy table.
The husband carries the table to the town.
The people see and praise the strong husband.
sentences.latin: Populus marītum fortem videt et laudat.

sentences.english: The wife's friend sees the strong husband.
But the friend envies the husband's courage.
In the town, the friend leads the husband to the rampart.
sentences.latin: In oppidō amīca marītum ad vallum dūcit.

sentences.english: The husband fortifies the great rampart.
And so the friend gives the husband a gift.
The friend believes the husband.
The wife praises her own husband.
The people praise the husband and the wife.
The husband and the wife are praised by the people.
sentences.latin: Marītus et uxor ā populō laudantur.

sentences.english: The wife opens the new book.
And so the husband loves his own strong wife.
sentences.latin: Itaque marītus uxōrem suam fortem amat.

sentences.english: In the school, the wise teacher teaches the grandson and the granddaughter.
sentences.latin: In scholā magister sapiēns nepōtem et neptem docet.

sentences.english: The wise grandson hears the wise teacher's beautiful and new song.
sentences.latin: Nepōs sapiēns magistrī sapientis pulchram et novam mūsam audit.

sentences.english: The wise teacher warns the strong granddaughter about the difficult song.
sentences.latin: Magister sapiēns neptem fortem dē mūsā difficilī monet.

sentences.english: The wise granddaughter tells the teacher all the difficult words of the song.
sentences.latin: Neptis sapiēns omnia verba difficilia mūsae magistrō dīcit.

sentences.english: And so the brave grandson and the wise granddaughter are praised by the wise teacher.
sentences.latin: Itaque nepōs fortis et neptis sapiēns ā magistrō sapientī laudantur.
